questions.q: What does SABSA stand for, and who originally created it?
options: Standard Architecture for Business Systems Assurance, published by ISO
Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture, created by practitioners John Sherwood, Andrew Clark, and David Lynas
Secure Architecture for Business Systems Auditing, created by NIST
Systematic Analysis of Business Security Attributes, created by The Open Group
questions.explain: SABSA is the Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture, created in the 1990s by working security architects John Sherwood, Andrew Clark, and David Lynas, and now maintained by the SABSA Institute.

questions.q: In SABSA's six-layer model, which layer sits at the very top and defines the business attributes security must serve?
options: Component
Physical
Logical
Contextual
questions.explain: The Contextual layer is the business itself — its goals, risk appetite, and the attributes (like availability or compliance) it needs from security — and every other layer traces back to it.

questions.q: What is SABSA's core, defining rule about any proposed security control?
options: It must trace back to a named business attribute, or it isn't really architecture
It must be certified by the SABSA Institute before implementation
It must be implemented at the Component layer before any other layer
It must cost less than 5% of the asset it protects
questions.explain: SABSA's defining principle is traceability: a control that can't be traced back to a real business requirement is just a control someone liked, not architecture.

questions.q: What are the "six W" questions SABSA asks at every layer of its matrix?
options: Risk, Cost, Time, Scope, Quality, Compliance
Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Authenticity, Non-repudiation, Accountability
What, Why, How, Who, Where, When
Plan, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, Operate
questions.explain: SABSA pairs its six layers with the six questions What, Why, How, Who, Where, and When, asked and re-answered at every single layer, producing the 36-cell SABSA Matrix.

questions.q: What is the Business Attributes Profile, and why does it matter in SABSA?
options: A product comparison matrix used to select security vendors
A stakeholder-defined list of business needs, like regulatory compliance or operational resilience, that every downstream control must serve
A list of IT department job titles mapped to security responsibilities
A technical inventory of every server and application in the environment
questions.explain: The Business Attributes Profile is built with business stakeholders, not IT, and becomes the yardstick every proposed control is measured against — it's what makes SABSA genuinely business-driven.
